newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour lead 10 to 22 points in opinion polls.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour lead 10 to 22 points in opinion polls.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party had leads ranging between 10 and 22 points over the ruling Conservatives in five opinion polls released on the eve of Thursday's election.
An ICM poll for Thursday's Guardian newspaper put support for Labour at 43 percent while the Conservatives were at 33 percent, giving Labour a 10-point lead.
The same poll recently gave Labour a lead of just five points, but this was dismissed as a freak because the opposition party has held double-digit leads throughout the six-week election campaign.
A Gallup poll for the Daily Telegraph gave Labour a 14-point lead with 47 percent of the vote, compared with 33 percent for the Conservatives.
The MORI poll for the Times newspaper put Labour 20 points ahead at 48 percent, while the Conservatives were at 28 percent.
An NOP poll for Reuters gave Labour a 22-point lead with 50 percent of the vote to the Conservatives' 28 percent.
And a Harris poll for the Independent newspaper gave Labour a 17-point lead, with 48 percent to the Conservatives' 31.
The polls gave the Liberal Democrats between 14 and 16 percent of the vote.
